transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... the main thing is I just get pulled off track by every little sound or thought. It's getting really frustrating. Like, I’ll be sitting there trying to work on a job application, and then a car goes by outside, or my phone buzzes, or even just some random idea pops into my head. And before I even notice what's happening, I've completely stopped what I was doing and I'm off doing something else. I just can't seem to stay on one thing.
How long has this difficulty with staying focused been going on? Has it always been this way, or did it start more recently?

Well, it hasn't always been this bad. It’s been really disruptive for about a year and 10 months now. It pretty much started getting this way after I had a soccer injury. That kind of knocked me out of my usual routine, and ever since then, it's just been a lot harder to keep my focus.
When you had that soccer injury, did you hit your head at all, or lose consciousness even for a moment?
No, nothing like that. It was just a torn ACL in my knee. I didn't hit my head or black out or anything. It was just a bad leg injury that kept me off the field and stuck at home for a long time.
Besides having trouble focusing, do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety, like you have a hard time sitting still?

Yeah, I do. Um... like, when I'm sitting down with someone, my leg is usually bouncing. Or I'll be clicking a pen, or just messing with my keys. I usually don't even realize I'm doing it until I catch myself. I just always have to be moving something.
Before you had that soccer injury about two years ago, did you have these kinds of focus and restlessness problems back when you were in school or as a younger person?

Yeah, actually. I mean, it wasn't exactly like it is now, but... yeah, even back in elementary school, I had issues. My teachers were always having to move my seat because I couldn't stop talking out of turn. And I was always forgetting my homework, or I'd just rush through my worksheets and make a bunch of careless mistakes. So, I guess the signs were there a long time ago.
